findings.finding: The submission did not provide one judge-facing trajectory packet or prove that every workflow agent had representative instructions, response, retry, verifier-feedback, and human-checkpoint evidence.
findings.repair: Generate AGENT_TRAJECTORIES.json and TRACE_INDEX.json from the canonical baseline, replay fixtures, contract-clarifier reports, and benchmark input trajectories; fail if the declared and observed workflow-agent sets differ.
validation: 24 baseline reviewer traces and provider fixtures are indexed
one approval and one rejection are embedded as representative baseline traces
the live/replay contract clarifier trace and deterministic feedback are embedded
synthetic repair trajectories are explicitly classified as untrusted inputs rather than workflow agents

findings.finding: Headline claims were spread across prose and result files without one machine-readable ledger binding the claim, evidence bytes, scope, and limitations.
findings.repair: Generate CLAIM_LEDGER.json with eight load-bearing claims, exact source paths, byte lengths, SHA-256 values, status, and material limitations.
validation: every claim is marked supported only after every evidence source is a regular file
metric claims are derived from the authoritative comparison
upstream attribution and benchmark limitations are explicit
submission drift detects a changed trace source

findings.finding: A judge had no direct map from the six scored criteria to evidence, claims, and executable checks.
findings.repair: Generate RUBRIC_MAP.json and JUDGE_CHECKLIST.md; require the six criteria to total exactly 100 points and bind the rubric to the claim-ledger hash.
validation: rubric criteria total exactly 100 points
every criterion references evidence-backed claim IDs
judge actions are paths or argument vectors rather than shell interpolation
the human checklist exposes the conservative approval/escalation trade-off

findings.finding: Release packaging copied only three submission entry points, so required trace and rubric evidence could be omitted from a downloaded delivery while the archives still verified.
findings.repair: Publish all eight submission entry points at the release root and in every archive, require them in HEAD, and verify their byte identity against release metadata and extracted archives.
validation: source, evidence, and full archives contain every judge-packet file
release root and archive copies are byte-identical
release manifest describes every delivery entry
unrelated release-root files remain fail-closed

findings.finding: An outer checksum alone could not prove that a rehashed trajectory replacement remained the packet bound by the trace index, claim ledger, rubric, and submission manifest.
findings.repair: Cross-verify trajectory, trace-index, claim-ledger, rubric, generated-file, and fixed-safety-boundary identities after outer checksum validation.
validation: a modified trajectory file with an updated SHA256SUMS entry is rejected
trace index binds trajectory byte length and SHA-256
rubric map binds the claim-ledger byte length and SHA-256
submission manifest binds every generated judge-packet file
